 By Staff Report | Hartford Courant Staff PUBLISHED: November 13, 2026 at 6:00 AM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... A New York attorney was sentenced for embezzling more than $500,000 from a trust he managed that involved a commercial building in Connecticut.
 Edward W. Miller, 71, of Lawrence, New York, was sentenced Thursday by U.S. District Judge Sarala V. Nagala in Hartford to eight months in prison followed by one year of supervised release, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Connecticut .
 Miller was an attorney licensed to practice law in New York. According to court records, an individual identified as “M.P.” established a trust in December 2014 for the purpose of managing certain property, including a commercial building in New Canaan.
 Miller was named as the trustee for the trust and was directed to open a trust bank account to manage the finances in the trust, “including depositing rental income from the commercial building into the trust account, paying costs associated with the management of the building and distributing funds to M.P.,” court records said.
 According to court records, Miller was also responsible for overseeing the maintenance of the building in the trust. The trust stated that Miller would be paid 5% of total monthly rents collected and any “agreed-upon commissions for new tenant leases and renewals.”
 Between February 2016 and September 2022, Miller reportedly embezzled more than $500,000 from the trust by writing unauthorized checks to himself, his law practice and his relatives, federal officials said. He also made unauthorized withdrawals and transfers from the trust bank account, according to federal officials.
 “After M.P. died in 2022, Miller made false representations and promises to M.P.’s beneficiaries about the identification, whereabouts, and disbursement of the trust’s assets,” federal officials said.
 On May 29, Miller pleaded guilty to wire fraud. According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office, he previously paid $509,372.82 in restitution as part of a settlement of a separate civil lawsuit filed by the victims.
 Miller is currently released on a $200,000 bond. He is required to report to prison on Jan. 11, 2027, the U.S. Attorney’s Office said.
